en.title: Minimum Operations When Two Items From Different Locations Can Ship Together
en.description:
In each operation, either ship any single item, or ship any two items from different locations together. The two items need not be adjacent; the remaining items keep their relative order, but that does not restrict the next free choice. Find the minimum number of operations to ship all items.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n and the second line contains locations. The original length is written as n in the body and as m in the constraints and starter; it is unified as n: 1≤n≤100000, 1≤locations[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 3, 2 and 2 respectively. In the first example only one 2 can be paired with a 1, and the other two 1s must ship alone.
hints: Let f be the highest frequency of a location; the answer is max(f,ceil(n/2)).
